The Ford Ranger family

6 generations and variants in the Index, 1983–present. Oldest first; every card opens the full page, with its own versions, figures and story.

  1. 1983–1992

    Ford Ranger (first generation)

    The first Ranger, 1983–1992: Ford's first compact pickup of its own design, and from 1987 the best-selling compact truck in America.

    73 hp14.8 sec 0-602,066,421 built
    2.0-liter 4-cylinder, manual · 2.3-liter 4-cylinder, 5-speed manual · 2.9-liter V6, automatic, 4x4
  2. 1993–1997

    Ford Ranger (second generation)

    The second Ranger, 1993–1997: smoother styling on the proven chassis, the Splash with its flared bed, and America's best-selling compact pickup throughout.

    160 hp8.9 sec 0-601,581,202 built
    4.0-liter V6 · 2.3-liter 4-cylinder, 5-speed manual · 3.0-liter V6
  3. 1998–2011

    Ford Ranger (third generation)

    The last of the compact Rangers, 1998–2011: a longer cab, new front suspension, a 4-door SuperCab, and production that ended in St. Paul in December 2011.

    207 hp8.1 sec 0-602,423,735 built
    4.0-liter V6, automatic, 4x4 · 2.3-liter 4-cylinder, 5-speed manual
  4. 2019–2023

    Ford Ranger (fourth generation)

    The Ranger's return, 2019–2023: the global midsize Ranger, built in Michigan, with a 270-hp turbo 4, a 10-speed and a 3,402-kg (7,500-lb) tow rating.

    270 hp6.0 sec 0-60375,151 built
    SuperCab, rear-wheel drive · SuperCrew, 4x4 · Tremor
  5. 2024–present

    Ford Ranger (fifth generation)

    The redesigned Ranger, 2024 on: a wider truck with a modern cabin, an optional 315-hp V6 and, in America, a SuperCrew only.

    270 hp6.2 sec 0-60117,165 built
    2.3-liter turbo 4-cylinder · 2.7-liter twin-turbo V6
  6. 2024–present

    Ford Ranger Raptor

    The first Ranger Raptor sold in America, 2024 on: 405 hp, FOX Live Valve shocks and a reinforced frame, built in Michigan.

    405 hp5.3 sec 0-60
